description: OpenTideConstants SDK API manifest (SDK spec section 4). Every public operation, attribute, argument, default, enum value and error code, by its snake_case name. Each SDK's CI turns the names into its own form by the naming rules below and compares them with its public surface; a missing or an extra name fails CI.

naming.ruby: methods and options snake_case; a predicate is_x is x?; an operation with mutating true ends in !; aliases.ruby are extra idiom names for the same operation
naming.python: snake_case; a predicate is_x is a property; options are keyword-only
naming.typescript: methods, predicates and options in camelCase: split the snake_case name on _, capitalise the first letter of each part after the first, join (station_by_alias -> stationByAlias, radius_km -> radiusKm, is_reference -> isReference getter); kind field members (data fields) keep snake_case; operations with typescript_async true return a Promise
naming.c: otc_ + snake_case; an operation's c gives its C function name(s) where the spec names them (a slash separates several functions); a field of an object with c type T is the accessor T_<field> (otc_station_lat), or a struct member when c_struct is true; enum values are OTC_<ENUM>_<VALUE> plus OTC_<ENUM>_OTHER; error codes map to otc_status values in errors[].c

kinds.attribute: a value with no args (Ruby method, Python property, TypeScript getter or property)
kinds.field: a data field with the schema's snake_case name in every language

after_close: After close, every call on the client or its Release (every query and every release-management operation; close itself excepted) raises io (FileError, message "the release is closed"), the same in eager and stream mode, and no automatic update runs (spec 4.2, 5.6, CR D21). This rule applies to every operation in this manifest, so it is stated once here and not added to each errors list.

client_options.note: Options of the client constructor (Ruby keyword arguments, Python keyword-only, TypeScript one options object, C otc_open_options / otc_fetch_options).

members.name: open

args.name: release
args.note: 'latest' or a datestamp matching ^[0-9]{8}(\.[2-9]|\.[1-9][0-9]{1,8})?$ (a counter of at most 9 digits); otherwise invalid_argument

args.name: file
args.note: open a local .json, .json.gz or .jsonl (+ .meta.json); TypeScript: Node only. The name must be OTC_<D><ext> (D a valid datestamp, ext one of these), otherwise invalid_argument; file together with release, offline or on_network_error is invalid_argument

args.name: cache_dir
args.note: null = platform cache directory (spec 5.4); env OPENTIDECONSTANTS_CACHE_DIR

args.name: offline
args.note: env OPENTIDECONSTANTS_OFFLINE: 1, true, yes or on (case-insensitive, trimmed) turns offline on; when it does, the env wins and an explicit offline false does not turn it off

args.name: base_url
args.note: env OPENTIDECONSTANTS_BASE_URL; checked at construction (C: at the first otc_fetch_* call): not an absolute http or https URL is invalid_argument, never retried, no cache fallback

args.name: proxy
args.note: null = HTTPS_PROXY / HTTP_PROXY / NO_PROXY, either case, except that upper-case HTTP_PROXY is ignored when REQUEST_METHOD is set (httpoxy); checked at construction: not an absolute http or https URL is invalid_argument, never retried, no cache fallback

args.name: ca_file
args.note: null = SSL_CERT_FILE, else the system store; checked at construction: a file that does not exist or cannot be read is io, never retried, no cache fallback

args.name: logger
args.note: Ruby logger:, Python the 'opentideconstants' logging logger, TypeScript {debug, info, warn}, C opts.log_fn

args.name: verify_on_open
args.note: hash the whole file on every open (spec 5.3)

members.note: Ruby OpenTideConstants.new(**options) and OpenTideConstants.open(**options) { |otc| }; Python OpenTideConstants(**options), usable as a context manager; TypeScript static async open(options) (a constructor cannot be async); C otc_open_file(path, &opts, &rel) opens a file only, and otc_fetch_latest / otc_fetch_release download first; a 200 pointer or index whose body is not JSON counts as a network error for on_network_error (spec 5.2 step 5); a failure to write the cached pointer is logged, not raised

members.name: last_error
members.note: the error behind loaded_from = cache_after_error; C: otc_last_error(rel, buf, len, &needed) gives the message of the last failure on the handle

members.name: releases
members.note: reads OTC_index.json; newest first

members.name: latest
members.note: reads the latest pointer (OTC_latest-f{MAJOR}.json, or OTC_latest.json on a 404) with a conditional GET, and OTC_index.json too when the pointer's release is not readable by this SDK (spec 5.2 steps 2 and 2a); does not switch release; offline: offline_unavailable, no socket

members.name: check_for_update
members.note: offline: offline_unavailable, no socket; sets newer_format_major from OTC_latest.json (spec 7.4)

members.name: newer_format_major
members.note: set by check_for_update from OTC_latest.json (never the per-major pointer): its format major when it is newer than every supported major, else null (spec 7.4). When check_for_update fails with unsupported_format or reader_too_old because only newer-major releases exist, it is set before the error is raised; on a network error it keeps its earlier value (not reset before the GET)

members.name: update
members.note: Ruby update!; a Release held from before stays valid; offline: offline_unavailable, no socket, and no switch to a newer cached release. C: otc_fetch_update(&fopts, current, path, len, &needed, &updated): needed gets the path length with its NUL; path and len are checked before any network access, so a small buffer is buffer_too_small and downloads nothing; updated is true only when the newer release is in the cache and path names it

members.name: download

args.name: formats
args.note: C: bit mask of OTC_FORMAT_JSON, OTC_FORMAT_JSON_GZ, OTC_FORMAT_JSONL; 0 = default

members.note: spec 4.3.2: writes the data files in formats plus OTC_{D}.sha256 and OTC_{D}.meta.json into to; returns the paths written (an identical existing file is not written and not listed); TypeScript in a browser fails with unsupported; C without otc_fetch returns OTC_E_NOT_BUILT; with release latest and a network error, on_network_error use_cache (the default) writes the newest cached readable release, raise (or no usable cached release) raises network; cache when the cache lock cannot be taken (a stale lock not removed after 3 attempts)

members.name: verify
members.note: hashes the files again in full against OTC_{D}.sha256; C otc_verify_file(path, sha256_path, &err) is in the core library; a client with loaded_from file_unverified has no OTC_{D}.sha256: checksum_mismatch, message "no OTC_{D}.sha256 next to the file"

errors.when: a lookup found nothing; Ruby/Python/TypeScript return nil/None/null, not an error
DNS, TLS, connection or timeout failure, or HTTP 5xx after the retries
offline mode and no usable cached release, or releases() offline and no cached index (a network failure with on_network_error raise is the network error)
a SHA-256 or size does not match, or the pointer and the .sha256 file disagree
the release's release.min_reader_version is newer than SUPPORTED_FORMAT_VERSION; the message names both versions
not JSON, a required field missing, or a reference does not resolve
update on a client opened on a pinned release or a file
download found a file in to with the same name and a different SHA-256, and overwrite is false
TypeScript in a browser: an operation that needs a file system (download)
a local file cannot be opened or read
a bad datestamp, lat or lon out of range, a negative radius, an empty query, or a NULL handle
C only; the needed size is in *needed or *count
C only: an otc_fetch_* or otc_predict_* call in a build without that module

error_base_class.note: every error class is a direct subclass of the base and of nothing else; every error has .code; a system error that causes an SDK error is kept as the cause

SUPPORTED_FORMAT_VERSION.note: the newest format version this SDK reads (spec 7.4); equals supported_format_version in the package's supported-formats.json

environment.OPENTIDECONSTANTS_OFFLINE: offline (1, true, yes or on, case-insensitive and trimmed; it wins over an explicit offline false)

reserved_phase2.note: Names reserved for the phase 2 prediction module (spec 4.9). Not built in phase 1: an SDK must not expose them yet, and the surface check ignores them.
